svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Antigenic shift in influenza A."], [1, "A human strain and a bird strain infect the same cell, for example in a pig."], [4, "Each releases its 8 RNA segments in the cell, where they are copied."], [7.5, "New virus particles package segments at random: reassortment."], [10.5, "One new virus has a new mix of H and N genes: a new strain few people are immune to."], [13, "Compare antigenic drift: small mutations, smaller changes."]]
svg.title: Antigenic shift
svg.desc: Two influenza A strains infect the same host cell, their eight RNA segments mix, and reassortment makes a new strain with a new combination of haemagglutinin and neuraminidase genes.
svg.text: Each virus has 8 RNA segments; H and N segments shown longer.

g.data-info: Influenza A has 8 separate RNA segments; two of them code for haemagglutinin (H) and neuraminidase (N).
A different strain with different H and N genes.
Pigs can be infected by both human and bird strains, so a pig cell can hold both at once.
g.text: host cell, e.g. in a pig

g.data-info: Segments from both strains are packaged together at random into new virus particles.
A new combination of H and N genes: few people have antibodies to it, so it can spread as a pandemic.
Small changes from point mutations in the H and N genes; the reason flu vaccines are updated each year.

g.text: Antigenic drift: point mutations in H and N genes
gradual small changes → flu vaccines updated every year
